proof.criterion: AC1: merge rule of the shared context on LINUX's replay
proof.surface: Dispatch server (packages/envoy/cmd/dispatch) built at base 59f6647d and head 8279d988 on local Postgres 17.11 + pgvector 0.8.7 and NATS 2.12.1 JetStream, driven by the INFRA-512 architect's replay (tools/load.py from infra512-replay-tools-tgz, replay-inputs.tar.gz sha256 4299570e...f42949, seed migrated once by the base build, 762-session fake listener)
proof.command: run1.sh <name> <bin>: fresh pg_restore, start Dispatch with GOMAXPROCS=2 and DISPATCH_PPROF_PORT, wait idle, python3 tools/load.py 0.3 1 27 8 (F=0.3, rho=1, 293 write events), utime+stime from /proc over the load, CPU profile 460 s; shares: go tool pprof -top -nodecount=1000000 -nodefraction=0 -edgefraction=0 '-focus=docs\.\(\*Service\)\.refreshAnchors$' <bin> <cpu.pb.gz>
proof.negativeControl: The base build under the same inputs uses 97-111 CPU-s more per run, and refreshAnchors is 24% of its CPU

proof.criterion: AC2a: identical anchor quotes, positions and results on real LINUX specs with many anchors
proof.surface: pmdoc test suite with the opt-in real-spec corpus (30 LINUX specs from the replay inputs' specs/: LINUX-364, -129, -43 and the 27 with the most open anchored comments; under $TMPDIR, never committed)
proof.observed: ok 990.549s; every test PASS; 121 marks per spec at 12/47/80, 0 specs skipped; FindMarks == FindMark+MarkAttrs, reused finder+writer gives bytes.Equal CRDT state, yTextRanges == frozen base copy
proof.negativeControl: FindMarks writing the separator at an empty marked run that ends the span fails TestFindMarksMatchesFindMarkOnHandBuiltTrees; leaf elements descended in yFragmentLocations fails the frozen-oracle tests; a MarkWriter reading its table before Update or dropping a Format fails TestReanchorReuseMatchesPerCall; FindDiscardingMiss returning nil fails TestQuoteFinderAnswersLikeFindQuote

proof.criterion: AC2b: refresh rows, events and order unchanged; refresh order now stable
proof.surface: docs, api and pmdoc suites on Postgres 17 + pgvector
proof.observed: docs ok (625 s). api fails only TestIssueRanksStayOrderedPastLowercaseDigitsAndProductionShapedMoves, which refuses a byte-order default collation; it passes on an ICU en-US cluster (ok 3.101s). pmdoc fails only three clock-ratio linearity tests, which fail identically at base 59f6647d. Everything else passes
proof.negativeControl: Without the ORDER BY in openAnchoredMarks, TestRefreshAnchorsAnnouncesEveryKindInRowOrder fails (round 0: row 0 listed ...d2, want ...d4); refreshing in the FindMarks map's order or one row per key fails the row-order and shared-mark tests; skipping only same-type rows fails TestAcceptSuggestionSkipsItsMarkIDForRowsOfEveryType

proof.criterion: AC2c: same anchors and versions after the replay
proof.surface: replay database at the end of a serial replay (tools/load_serial.py: the same tool with one worker and no pacing, so its shared random draws happen in log order) at base twice and at head
proof.command: ENDSTATE=1 LOAD=tools/load_serial.py run1.sh sbase1|sbase2 <base bin>, shead2 <head bin>; dump every anchored comment and ask (kind, issue, body, quote, orphaned, state) as JSON rows and each document's latest version (number, md5 of markdown)
proof.observed: 3,476 anchor rows identical as multisets in sbase1, sbase2 and shead2; the latest version of all 1,165 documents identical
proof.negativeControl: The concurrent tool (96 threads sharing one random.Random) gives different end states between two base runs (84 of 1,165 latest versions differ), so a comparison without the serial run cannot tell variance from a change

proof.criterion: AC3: a write's cost no longer grows with open anchored comments at 10, 40 and 80
proof.surface: BenchmarkAnchoredWrite (docs, Postgres, ~150 KB document, N open anchored comments the write leaves unchanged) and BenchmarkFindMarks (pmdoc)
proof.command: go test ./internal/dispatch/docs/ -run '^$' -bench BenchmarkAnchoredWrite -benchmem -count=5 -benchtime=3x at head and at base (the same file in a 59f6647d tree); go test ./internal/dispatch/pmdoc/ -run '^$' -bench BenchmarkFindMarks -benchmem -count=5
proof.observed: head N80/N10 medians (ns, B/op, allocs): doc-edit 0.99 / 0.98 / 1.02, anchored comment 0.97 / 1.02 / 1.03, upload 1.07 / 1.03 / 1.03; FindMarks ns 1.05 (150 KB) and 1.13 (400 KB)
proof.negativeControl: Base fails the line: doc-edit 3.79 / 4.74 / 3.88, anchored comment 4.44 / 5.11 / 4.42, upload 5.37 / 7.01 / 5.81; the per-key FindMark loop grows 7.2x and 8.3x

proof.criterion: AC4: no memory the server keeps resident
proof.surface: the diff and the replay's heap profiles at the window's end
proof.observed: inuse_space base 802 / 810 / 794 MB, head 720 / 808 / 787 MB (within the base runs' range); no new field on Service, a room, a replica or liveWrite and no package variable holding document data
proof.negativeControl: Base runs differ among themselves by 16 MB, the variance the head is judged against

trickyParts: FindMarks reproduces FindMark's quote walk exactly, including empty marked runs: one is written only when a later run of the same span carries the span past it.
yFragmentLocations mirrors walk's arithmetic for elements named text, doc and leaf types, and keeps every structural refusal ahead of the alignment refusals.

MarkWriter reads yTextRanges once, after MarkRange's own checks, and relies on Format changing no text length or element structure; the re-anchor test checks the cached table against a fresh one after every mark.
deviations: MarkQuote's 'written mark is missing' ErrDocSchema refusal now fires after applyLive's append and version write instead of inside the callback (plan decision 3); the caller's transaction rolls back on it, and it is reachable only on a pmdoc position bug.
openAnchoredMarks gained ORDER BY created_at, id at the INFRA-512 architect's request (defect found by INFRA-642's implementer), so refresh event order is now stable rather than unchanged.
AC2c used a serial copy of the replay tool, because the tool's shared random generator makes two concurrent base runs differ.
